newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai soybean futures mixed in slow trading.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai soybean futures mixed in slow trading.

text.p: Shanghai soybean futures ended mixed in slow trading on Monday on profit-taking after Friday's rises, traders said.
The key March 1997 contract ended at 3,197 yuan ($385) per tonne, losing three yuan. It opened at an intra-day low of 3,150 and hit a high of 3,210.
May fell 107 to 3,101, July 34 to 3,245, September put on eight to 3,286, November 14 to 3,384.
Combined volume fell to 19,600 tonnes from 25,100.
"Profit-taking emerged at high price levels with few investors buliding long positions with the approach of the Chinese new year holiday," one trader said.
"Investors opt for quick profits instead of long-term positions in this sort of situation," he added.
Analysts said they expected soybeans to move in a narrow range in the short term.
